findings.reason: The protected solution is already the conventional duplicate-free backtracking method: constrain factors to nondecreasing order, scan only through the square root of each remainder, emit the quotient completion, and recurse to split that quotient further. Its concept names and structure are expert interview-quality, so no candidate is justified.

The app-local and immutable Accepted native sources have identical search parameters, divisor bound, divisibility test, emitted paths, recursive transition, and return order; only collection typing syntax and the required LeetCode class-method wrapper differ.

The legal increasing-prime tiers 1,009/10,007/100,003 isolate unsuccessful divisor-search growth without output cost. The current source passes at -0.00 relative exponent with a 1.03x largest runtime ratio; a correct implementation that scans factors through the full remainder passes every output and fails only scaling at +0.67 with a 152.26x ratio.

The Approach proves completeness through the smallest-factor square-root bound and uniqueness through nondecreasing paths, states the output-sensitive and recursion-depth costs, and now labels prime/tiny inputs and repeated factors separately.

The hash-bound Premium Reference remains verified against the source structure, preserving all three factual examples, the nontrivial-factor range, arbitrary output order, and the sole numeric constraint.
